name: Magnolias and tulip trees
status: 4 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: Magnolias are beetle-pollinated — the oldest flowering-plant pollination on Earth — with big cream, white or pink cups; the ledger's beetle count sets their seed. Fruit cones with red seeds taken by birds. Asian, Himalayan, eastern North American and a few tropical species.

canopy.name: Southern magnolia

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two fleshy oblong cotyledons, then glossy evergreen leaves, smaller and thinner than the adult's and less rusty-felted beneath. The sapling is a dense, pyramidal evergreen with a single straight leader and branches down to the ground (46-61 cm in its first year in a nursery). It endures shade for years; flowers start at about 10 years.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 2 (Magnolia grandiflora: seed from age 10, optimum ~25; nursery seedlings 46-61 cm in year 1; 18-24 m at 80-120 yr; tolerant of shade when young); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (epigeal, germination in 30-50 days after stratification)

repro.note: beetle-pollinated: reads the ledger's beetle count, not bees

canopy.source: SE US coastal plain; 20–30 m. Glossy evergreen; huge cream flowers. Kew POWO for the name; standard floras for range.

canopy.name: Yulan magnolia

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two thick oval cotyledons, then alternate obovate leaves with a short abrupt tip. Young trees are single-stemmed and upright with a narrow, open crown of stout grey twigs; furry grey flower buds appear only after several years, and the crown rounds out with age.
growth.source: PFAF (10 m, slow growing; beetle pollinated; seed ripe Sep-Nov, needs cold stratification, can take 18 months); Missouri Botanical Garden Plant Finder; age at first flowering and lifespan estimated (old temple trees in China are centuries old)

repro.note: beetle-pollinated: reads the ledger's beetle count, not bees

canopy.name: Campbell's magnolia

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two thick oval cotyledons, then alternate, large soft oblong leaves. The sapling is a vigorous single-leadered, rather narrow upright tree (shoots up to ~1.2 m a year) with stout grey twigs; the big furry flower buds are absent for the first 15-30 years, and the crown only broadens into a spreading dome with age.
growth.source: PFAF (at least 20 yr from seed to flower; beetle pollinated; seed needs winter cold, may take 18 months); T. Stone 'Plant of the week' (15 yr white forms to 30 yr pink forms from seed, ~10 yr grafted; young trees add up to 4 ft/yr); Wikipedia (30 m, rarely 45; flowers 15-25 cm); lifespan estimated

canopy.name: Tulip tree

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two narrow, oblong cotyledons, then the unmistakable square-ended, four-lobed 'tulip' leaves on a straight green stem. In full light seedlings bolt from their second year and may be 3-5.5 m tall at five years: a straight, slender, grey-green whip with a narrow conical crown. Stump sprouts grow even faster, about 1.4 m a year.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 2 (Liriodendron tulipifera: 70-90 day stratification, epigeal; 3-5.5 m at 5 yr; site index 30 m: 15.8 m at 20 yr, 27 m at 40, 32 m at 60, 37 m at 100; flowers at 15-20 yr; 30-46 m mature, to 61 m; lives 200-250, up to 300 yr; shade-intolerant).

repro.note: beetle-pollinated: reads the ledger's beetle count, not bees
